title: Constitution sets up institutions
description: Parliamentary system, independent judiciary, and an executive accountable to the legislature become the foundation of governance.

title: Parliament and law-making
description:
Elected representatives debate policies, pass laws, approve budgets, and scrutinize the executive.
	Committees and question hour strengthen accountability.

title: Government ministries and implementation
description: The Council of Ministers (with the Prime Minister) runs departments; the civil service supports administration and implements decisions.

title: Judiciary and rule of law
description:
Courts interpret the Constitution, protect fundamental rights, and review government actions.
	Judicial independence is essential for democracy.

title: Coalitions and institutional coordination
description: When no single party has a clear majority, coalition politics increases negotiation inside the cabinet and Parliament, shaping how decisions are made.

title: Institutions make democracy work daily
description:
Democracy depends on procedures and institutions, not just ideals.
	Key ideas: accountability, transparency, checks and balances, and citizens' participation through their representatives.
